articles.summary: Simply Wall St.: How Royal Caribbean’s New Tri‑Branded Credit Cards With Bank of America Could Shape RCL’s Investor Story. Royal Caribbean Group and Bank of America have launched the Royal ONE and Royal ONE Plus Visa Signature tri-branded credit cards, allowing guests to earn and redeem rewards across Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea with tiered point multipliers, travel perks, and no foreign transaction fees. This tri-branded program deepens Royal Caribbean’s loyalty ecosystem by tying everyday card spending directly to cruise savings and onboard experiences across its three core brands. Next,... articles.title: Gulf Funds Agree to Back Paramount’s $81 Billion Takeover of Warner
articles.mainIdea: Gulf Funds Agree to Back Paramount’s $81 Billion Takeover of Warner
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: Gulf Funds Agree to Back Paramount’s $81 Billion Takeover of Warner. Paramount has received signed equity commitments of close to $24 billion from three sovereign-wealth funds led by Saudi Arabia to help back its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery according to people familiar with the matter. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund has agreed to provide roughly $10 billion of the nearly $24 billion to Paramount, run by David Ellison, the son of billionaire Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison. The agreements with investors also include Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi’s L’imad Holding Co., the people said. Related tickers mentioned: ORCL, PSKY, WBD.
